claims.text: In Dart, a comment starting with /// directly above a declaration is a documentation comment for that declaration.
claims.source_hint: dart.dev: Effective Dart: Documentation (doc comments); Dart language: Comments > Documentation comments

claims.text: With the cursor on a widget's constructor call, the Flutter tools in VS Code or Android Studio (Flutter Property Editor) can show that widget's /// documentation, including for the app's own widgets. Square brackets in a doc comment reference in-scope names so doc tools can link them.
claims.source_hint: Flutter docs: Tools > Flutter Property Editor (widget documentation, custom widgets); Effective Dart: Documentation (square brackets for in-scope identifiers)

claims.text: At stage-3 StatusBanner's /// comment states its purpose, example cases (saved list out of date, waiting order, server error), says it is not for a screen with nothing else to show (use MessageView) and that it takes a tone, never a color; it lists no parameters.
At stage-3 LoadingView and MessageView also carry /// comments saying what they are for and when not to use them; MessageView's is for a whole screen with nothing else to show.

`flutter run -d chrome -t lib/gallery_main.dart` runs the app in Chrome starting from that file's main; -t (--target) names the main entry-point file and defaults to lib/main.dart, for flutter run and flutter build web alike.
claims.source_hint: flutter run --help / flutter build web --help: --target (-t), 'Defaults to lib/main.dart'; Flutter docs: flutter CLI

claims.text: The Dart web compiler builds main.dart.js only from the libraries reachable through imports from the entry point; a file nothing imports is not compiled into the output, and tree shaking further leaves out code that is not called.
claims.source_hint: dart.dev: dart compile js (dart2js) — compiles from an entry point, tree shaking; Flutter docs: Build and release a web app

claims.text: At stage-3 the only file under DonHang.App/lib with an import line containing 'gallery' is lib/gallery_main.dart (it imports gallery/examples.dart); nothing imports gallery_main.dart. `grep -rl "import.*gallery" lib` prints only lib/gallery_main.dart.
claims.source_hint: examples/don-hang @ stage-3: git grep -l -E 'import.*gallery' -- DonHang.App/lib (only lib/gallery_main.dart:6)

claims.text: gallery_main.dart has its own main and MaterialApp (title, theme, home) using buildTheme(donHangBrand, Brightness.light) and a ListView, one _section per entry. buildTheme turns a Brand and Brightness into ThemeData; donHangBrand holds seed and status colors; main.dart makes the same call.
claims.source_hint: examples/don-hang @ stage-3: DonHang.App/lib/gallery_main.dart:13-31; lib/design/theme.dart:11; lib/design/brand.dart:24; lib/main.dart:39-40

claims.text: _section shows the example's name above two copies of its widget side by side; _inTheme wraps each copy in a Theme built by buildTheme for Brightness.light or Brightness.dark, on that theme's surface color.
A Theme widget gives its subtree the ThemeData passed as data; Theme.of(context) below it returns that data instead of MaterialApp's theme.
claims.source_hint: Flutter API: material library, Theme class, Theme.of

claims.text: galleryExamples at stage-3 holds 8 GalleryExample entries (name + widget): loading_view, message_view, message_view_action, status_banner_info/success/warning/error (one per StatusTone value, four tones) and status_banner_action (error tone with an action).

The comment on galleryExamples says the same list feeds the gallery, the accessibility test (both themes) and the image-comparison test, so a new variant added there is shown and tested without changing those files.
When the gallery runs the same widget code as the app, a component change shows the next time it runs, while a separate written page with screenshots stays at the old look until someone updates it.

Documenting a component well needs its purpose, when not to use it and its look, not a second list of its parameters; the first two fit a /// comment, the look a gallery. Both sit next to the code, so the pull request changing a component can update them in the same diff.

When some component states appear only after rare events (rejected order, changed price) and the app shows one theme at a time, a gallery showing every entry in both themes catches look changes the real app hides.
git switch --detach <tag> checks out the commit a tag points to without creating a branch.
Running the gallery opens a page titled 'DonHang.App components' with eight sections, each showing the component on a light surface (left) and a dark surface (right).
claims.source_hint: examples/don-hang @ stage-3: DonHang.App/lib/gallery_main.dart:20-65; run flutter run -d chrome -t lib/gallery_main.dart

claims.text: At stage-3 StatusColors is a ThemeExtension holding warning and success colors; warning-tone StatusBanners appear for the out-of-date saved list, a queued order whose price changed, and a sync paused by a rate limit or a needed sign-in.
